subject: horizontal pod autoscaler of the gateway service observed on a real kubernetes cluster

verdict.summary: The gateway-service horizontal pod autoscaler raised the deployment from 2 to 10 replicas while a k6 load of 600 requests per second hit the gateway actuator endpoint, and returned it to 2 replicas after the load stopped.

metrics_server.local_adjustment: the deployment args were patched with --kubelet-insecure-tls because the kind kubelet serves a self signed certificate
metrics_server.verification: kubectl top nodes and kubectl top pods returned values for the gateway pods

manifests_applied: k8s/workload-protection.yaml (the shop-system service account and the gateway-service pod disruption budget only)

auxiliary_dependency.name: redis
auxiliary_dependency.reason: the gateway edge rate limiter calls redis and fails closed with 503 when redis is unreachable
auxiliary_dependency.source: uncommitted auxiliary manifest applied from /tmp, not part of the audited k8s directory

secrets.values: random local only values generated outside the repository, the template file keeps its placeholders and no real value was committed

load_profile_environment.source: the load test profile of the repository, docker-compose.loadtest.yml
load_profile_environment.reason: the committed rate limits of 50 requests per second per client would have capped the load below the autoscaling threshold
load_profile_environment.applied_with: kubectl set env deployment/gateway-service, applied before the baseline snapshot and the rolling restart was allowed to settle

load.generator: k6 v2.4.0 (grafana/k6 image) running as a job inside the cluster
load.scenario: constant arrival rate against the public actuator endpoint of the gateway
load.note: the dropped iterations show that the gateway was the bottleneck of the run, the load was not limited by the generator

before_load.note: the autoscaler had already moved the deployment from the 3 replicas of the manifest down to its minimum of 2

under_load.note: the load was concentrated on the pods that already held the client connections, the horizontal pod autoscaler reacted to the average utilisation of the deployment

after_load.note: the scale down ran through the default 300 second stabilisation window and ended at the minimum of 2 replicas

event_driven_autoscaling.detail: the k8s directory declares no event driven autoscaler, the only autoscaler is the horizontal pod autoscaler of the gateway in k8s/gateway-service.yaml, and there is no KEDA ScaledObject or equivalent
event_driven_autoscaling.verdict: not verified, the platform declares no event driven autoscaler to verify
